title: Morning Edition
intro: Google updated its frontier model line with Gemini 4 Carbon, and outlets are already parsing its security and coding claims. Other stories cover small-business AI tools, a personal experiment with an AI death predictor, and the physical infrastructure powering modern AI.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a ‘significant leap’ in cybersecurity
items.summary: Google has released its latest frontier model, Gemini 4 Carbon, offering "significant gains" in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In an announcement on Wednesday, Google highlights Carbon's top spot on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0) benchmark, with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind. The new Gemini 4 Carbon model offers improvements over […]
items.why: A top-ranked frontier model shifts competitive positioning among large AI labs and signals new capability claims for security and coding.
items.headline: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon
items.aiSummary: Google released Gemini 4 Carbon and said it delivers significant gains in coding, agentic tasks, and cybersecurity. In a Wednesday announcement Google highlighted Carbon topping the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5.0), with Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra trailing behind.

items.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Carbon: The Future of Cybersecurity Unveiled
items.summary: Discover how Google’s Gemini 4 Carbon is set to revolutionize cybersecurity. Explore its cutting-edge features, advanced AI capabilities, and the impact it will have on protecting digital assets in the ever-evolving landscape of online threats.
items.why: Business-focused coverage frames the model as relevant to companies concerned about cyber risk and AI features.
items.headline: Coverage positions Gemini 4 Carbon for cybersecurity
items.aiSummary: Small Business Trends ran a feature presenting Gemini 4 Carbon as having major implications for cybersecurity and advanced AI capabilities. The piece frames the model as important for protecting digital assets and tracking changes in online threats.

items.title: Pax8 launches 8os & 8bot for small business partners
items.why: New tooling for partners may affect how small-business IT services are delivered and automated.
items.headline: Pax8 launches 8os and 8bot for partners
items.aiSummary: Pax8 announced two new products, 8os and 8bot, aimed at small business partners. The launch targets the company’s channel audience rather than general consumers.

items.title: I Gave My Blood to the AI Death Clock
items.summary: Death Clock promises to predict when you’re going to die and help you extend your time on Earth. After a month, I felt like it was sucking the life out of me.
items.why: A personal test highlights the psychological effects of predictive health tools that claim to forecast mortality.
items.headline: I gave my blood to the AI death clock
items.aiSummary: Wired’s reporter tried a service called Death Clock that promises to predict when you’ll die and to help you extend your lifespan. After a month using the product the writer said the experience felt like it was sucking the life out of them.

items.title: AI has come for Arizona’s water
items.summary: A hulking gray giant rises from the desert. Inside, engineers create the force behind our phones and computers and appliances, our streaming services and search engines and chatbots and vibe-coded apps and websites. The complex is simultaneously massive and squat, dwarfed by the mountains that surround it, and it is endless. I drive past one […]
items.why: Reporting ties large physical AI infrastructure to everyday digital services and regional resources like water.
items.headline: AI has come for Arizona’s water
items.aiSummary: The Verge describes a massive data center rising from the desert where engineers build systems that power phones, computers, streaming services, search engines, chatbots and apps. The complex is described as both massive and squat, dwarfed by surrounding mountains.
